caption: The drawing is a technical design of a furniture piece, likely a cabinet or secretary desk, rendered in black ink on a light, aged background. The structure has an ornate decorative finial at the top left and right corners, with curved and floral embellishments topping the central section. The upper section contains two large doors, the left one featuring two rectangular glass panels with fan-shaped decorations at the top and bottom corners, and the right, a solid panel. The lower section is divided into two vertical halves: the left side displays four horizontally aligned drawers, each fitted with two handles in a decorated style, while the right side shows areas with vertical and horizontal divisions suggesting cubbyholes or compartments, and outlines for possible drawers or sliding panels. Flanking the central structure, both sides feature vertical, fluted columns. The rightmost part includes a side view with measurements indicated, showing the depth of the structure and labeled "SLIDE SUPPORT" near the bottom. The entire drawing is annotated with measurements and scale (⅛ inch to 1 inch), and some decorative elements such as shell motifs and scrollwork are present in the panels and trims. The feet of the piece are cabriole-style with a shaped skirt, and the base stretches 40 inches wide. The designer’s name, W.W. Jennings, appears at the bottom right.
